summary: After Cana, Jesus goes down to Capernaum with His mother, His brothers and His disciples, and they stay there only a few days.
key_insight: John names who traveled with Jesus: His mother, His brothers and His disciples, family and followers together. It will not stay that way. A few chapters later John writes, “For even His brothers did not believe in Him” (7:5).
story: After the wedding, Jesus went down from Cana to Capernaum, on the shore of the Sea of Galilee.
His mother, His brothers and His disciples went with Him.
They did not stay there many days. The Passover was near, and Jesus would soon go up to Jerusalem.

scene.label: Down to Capernaum
scene.text: Cana sat in the hills of Galilee. Capernaum lay on the northwest shore of the Sea of Galilee, about 700 feet below sea level, so the road ran downhill. It was a fishing town, and Simon and Andrew, who came from Bethsaida (John 1:44), had a house there (Mark 1:21, 29).

scene.label: His brothers
scene.text: Mark names four brothers, James, Joses, Judas and Simon, and mentions sisters (Mark 6:3). Christians understand “brothers” in different ways. Most Protestants see them as later children of Joseph and Mary; the Eastern Orthodox tradition sees them as Joseph’s children by an earlier marriage; Roman Catholic teaching sees them as close relatives such as cousins. Views differ.

scene.label: Where is Joseph?
scene.text: Joseph is not mentioned after Jesus’ boyhood. Many conclude that he had died by this time, though the Gospels do not say.

scene.label: Jesus’ later home
scene.text: After leaving Nazareth, Jesus made Capernaum His home (Matthew 4:13), and Matthew calls it “His own city” (Matthew 9:1). This short visit was the first of many.

witnesses.john: Only John mentions this brief stay. It links the sign at Cana to the first Passover, and John even notes that the stay was short, the kind of detail an eyewitness remembers. It is also the first glimpse of Capernaum, the town the other Gospels make Jesus’ base in Galilee.

seeing.reveals: Jesus did not cut Himself off from His family to begin His work. For a time the Son of God traveled with His mother, His brothers and His new disciples, living as a son and brother.
seeing.living: The brothers who walked beside Jesus here would later doubt Him, and yet after the resurrection they were found praying with the disciples (Acts 1:14). Being near Jesus is not yet faith, but God is patient with families. Keep bringing yours into His company and keep praying.
seeing.ponder: Who in your family is near Jesus but not yet trusting Him, and how will you keep praying for them?

preaching.big_idea: Close to Jesus is not the same as trusting Him, but He does not give up on family.
outline: Disciples who saw His glory and believed (11)
A family who walked beside Him (12)
Near Him is not yet trusting Him (12; compare 7:5)
A patience that waited for the brothers (12; compare Acts 1:14)
preaching.watch_for: John often notes short moves and stays (2:12; 4:40, 43; 11:54). These notes of time and place read like an eyewitness’s memory and tie Jesus’ signs to real towns and days.
